findings.where: Article specimen: the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' and its byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024', at both widths
findings.fault: The byline sits almost on the title's descenders, only a few pixels below them, and then a full line of space opens before the body. Everywhere else the article keeps an even 32 px rhythm. Here the byline looks jammed under the title instead of belonging to it, and the article's opening looks unfinished.
findings.who_objects: The founder, and Angélique when she publishes articles. The specimen is meant to show a rhythm that holds when content is added, and its first join is the one hand-tight gap. A reader opening Mark's article sees a cramped title block before the first line.

findings.where: First screen, nav: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark, at both widths
findings.fault: Mark's name is set small, about 20 px, in regular-weight serif, roughly the size of the nav links. The arch mark beside it outweighs it, and the 80 px headline dwarfs it. At first glance the logo leads and the name reads as a caption to it.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test asks for his name to lead with the logo beside it. A development-bank visitor should register Mark first, not the firm, and here the type says the firm.

findings.where: Article specimen: the PDF list entry 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge / Lecture · 23 April 2026', at both widths
findings.fault: The entry's title and date start about 4 px to the right of the article's left edge, so they don't line up with the body text above. The title is also set at body size on the body's loose 32 px line, so the two-line title reads as one more paragraph rather than an item in a list of documents.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning down to the PDFs, which the research calls the product. The entry doesn't read as a distinct item, and the slight indent looks like a mistake.

findings.where: Mark's name in the header compared with the footer ('Mark M. Moseley · Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com')
findings.fault: The same name, used as the same kind of identity, is set in the serif in the header and in Public Sans in the footer. Like text is set unlike.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging the identity. The name is the brand, and it should keep one face everywhere it signs the page.
